title: autotune: default batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Raman
description: Context: This PR implements the first end-to-end pass of automated cost-optimization defaults for serving: (1) default batching and KV-prefix caching heuristics, (2) model quantization profile templates and safe rollout hooks, and (3) a small unit-economics toolkit that surfaces per-request token cost estimates and recommendations. Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for opinionated defaults that reduce token cost without manual tuning. The goal is to provide safe defaults plus an autotune flow operators can opt into, and observability into unit economics so teams can measure benefit. What changed: 1) Runtime: added batch_policy v2 that derives target batch size from recent latency percentiles, sequence-length distributions and customer latency SLOs; integrated prefix KV caching with LRU/time-decay heuristics and configurable TTLs; exposed new per-route hints (preferred_batch, cache_policy). 2) Quantization: added quant_profiles v1 (fp16, int8-symmetric, int8-asymmetric, gptq-8bit) with metadata about expected throughput and measured quality delta across our eval-suite; safe-rollout hook that runs a held-out promptset to validate regressions before promotion. 3) Unit economics: new CLI command redwood uecon estimate and a small UI panel that shows per-route token-cost, estimated savings from batching/quantization, and confidence bands. 4) Tooling/tests/docs: end-to-end integration tests, new benchmark harness scripts for autotune scenarios, migration guide and docs. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool, monitor latency and quality evals for 48h, automatic rollback on SLO or quality regression thresholds. Checklist: - [x] Runtime batching/caching implementation - [x] Quant profiles and eval harness - [x] UEcon CLI and simple console panel - [x] Integration tests and perf benchmarks - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Canary + rollback policy Related work: ENG-3421 (autotune controller), ENG-3487 (quant onboarding), PM-211 (pricing & observability requirements). Notes: quant_profiles include conservative default mappings per GPU family; users can opt out or pin older profiles. This PR intentionally keeps the autotuner disabled by default and wires the recommendation engine into the console, not auto-applying changes without explicit operator approval.

review_comments: Ben Liu: Overall looks good. Two requests: (1) make the default cache TTL configurable per customer level, not only route-level; (2) add a flow metric for batches dropped due to SLO violation. Can you add unit tests for the TTL behavior?

Aisha Raman (author): Added customer-level TTL override and added unit tests (tests/cache/ttl_override.test). Also added a dashboard tile for 'batches_dropped_slo' in console. See commit d4a8e9c and e5b9f0d.

Carlos Mendes: Concern about int8 symmetric profile on older Ampere cards causing hallucination increase in our eval set (+1.6% F1 drop). Please gate that profile behind the safe-rollout and default to fp16 for p3/p4 families.

Aisha Raman (author): Good catch; quant_profiles.yaml now maps int8-asymmetric as the conservative option for Ampere and forces fp16 as default. Added evaluation artifacts and noted expected quality delta in profile metadata.
Priya Kapoor: Add documentation on how to opt out and pin model/quant profiles (security/compliance required). Also confirm that KMS/RBAC checks are enforced for private deployments.
Aisha Raman (author): Added docs/migrations/2026-02-autotune.md section 'pinning-and-compliance' and added RBAC check in serving controller (serving/src/acl/checks.rs).

benchmarks: throughput +18% on batchy workloads, latency median +3ms
release_notes: Introduce autotune defaults: new batching/caching defaults, quantization profile templates (v1), and a unit-economics estimation tool. Autotuner is opt-in; safe-rollout hooks enforce quality checks before applying quant profiles. See docs/migrations/2026-02-autotune.md for migration steps.
pr_summary: Implements opt-in autotune defaults for batching and prefix caching, introduces quantization profiles with safe-rollout evaluation, and ships a small unit-economics toolkit in CLI and Console. Includes tests, docs, and a staged canary plan.
